title: S145 19.1.1 SIP and SIPS URI Components
parent_path: S145 19.1.1 SIP and SIPS URI Components

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The userinfo part of a URI is optional and MAY be absent when the destination host does not have a notion of users or when the host itself is the resource being identified.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the @ sign is present in a SIP or SIPS URI, the user field MUST NOT be empty.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the host being addressed can process telephone numbers, for instance, an Internet telephony gateway, a telephone-subscriber field defined in RFC 2806 [9] MAY be used to populate the user field.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: While the SIP and SIPS URI syntax allows this field to be present, its use is NOT RECOMMENDED, because the passing of authentication information in clear text (such as URIs) has proven to be a security risk in almost every case where it has been used.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Implementations not wishing to give special significance to the password portion of the field MAY simply treat "user:password" as a single string.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Using the fully-qualified domain name form is RECOMMENDED whenever possible.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Even though an arbitrary number of URI parameters may be included in a URI, any given parameter-name MUST NOT appear more than once.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: For a SIPS URI, the transport parameter MUST indicate a reliable transport.
actions: set transport parameter to a reliable transport protocol when constructing SIPS URI

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The ttl parameter determines the time-to-live value of the UDP multicast packet and MUST only be used if maddr is a multicast address and the transport protocol is UDP.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the user string contains a telephone number formatted as a telephone-subscriber, the user parameter value "phone" SHOULD be present.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Even without this parameter, recipients of SIP and SIPS URIs MAY interpret the pre-@ part as a telephone number if local restrictions on the name space for user name allow it.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Since the uri-parameter mechanism is extensible, SIP elements MUST silently ignore any uri-parameters that they do not understand.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Elements processing URIs SHOULD ignore any disallowed components if they are present.
